Problem description
- A customer tried to charge his EV, but the charge stopped after 5 minutes. There were 3 attempts, but the same LOGS message was still displayed: "Outlet=DC2|CableName=EV-T2M4CC DC|EventType=Warn|Tdiff(degC)=14.9|Contact1(degC)=40.3|Contact2(degC)=25.4|Power(kW)=83.4|Current(A)=221.0|Energy(kWh)=5.5|"
Additional info from customer-
We have several cases of this type at several charging stations, with several tickets regarding a potential cable heating issue. Please provide us with a reliable answer so we can justify ourselves to our customers
Logs collected & attached below. Need to be discussed with ES Team.

additional_info.subject: ID0416297-DC/Si-D/FR-[Y2 / P0 312567479/03] DC2_CableTempSensor_XD101 CRM:00921001662
additional_info.body:
Hello Gregory, good morning. I hope you are doing well.
This error was due to a mismatch between temperature sensors of the plug. In the firmware version v6.0.3 the limit is 15ºC, when this limit is triggered, the session is stopped and the plug unavailable until the sensors are, again, below 15ºC difference.
In the latest firmware version v6.1.3 this is mitigated by increasing the limit value.
My recommendation is to, first, update the charger to the latest version and see if it's fixed. Otherwise we need to send a Siemens representative to do troubleshooting.
I will wait patiently for your feedback.
Best regards,
Francisco

additional_info.subject: ID0416297-DC/Si-D/FR-[Y2 / P0 312567479/03] DC2_CableTempSensor_XD101 CRM:00921001662
additional_info.body:
PS:
Please include photos of the DC plug including the pins, we want to see if there is any signs of damage that can cause this temperature to increase.
Thank you very much!
Best regards,
Francisco

Dear Colleagues,
Mr. Gregory from Engie raised this ticket regarding CableTempSensor issue. From the logs we see the 15ºC difference between + and - . In the v6.1.3 this limit is raised and possibly fixes the situation. If not, please move to site and do a thorough visual check on the DC pins. It seems that the customer disabled the outlet on purpose but the error flag is not present, so I am removing a KF14 or bad-measurement from the picture.
